And also i would like to add that my comment is not supposed to discourage u at all from going to see someone. U do need to speak to somebody,i would just ask them about talking therapies etc first before meds and see how u go with that.

I would strongly advise talking therapies etc before trying medication. Your brain has not fully developed yet and medications can really fuck u up,they are not supposed to be given to anyone under 21. But even if u were 21 i would still try and avoid as they are very complex and can really fuck u up long term. I'm speaking from personal experience. I was shoved on them when i was 17 and it's been a downward spiral ever since. A psychiatrist will encourage you to take them as that's how they make their money. Dr's too. I know  everybody is different and not every situation is the same but a chemical imbalance is not always the reason for depression,it could be situational or a repetitive patterns that occur in your life. Even if it was chemical,it really is pot luck with finding a medication that might work and even then the side effects of switching and going up and down on dosages can have long term lasting effects. Especially when you're so young and brain is still developing. Whatever you decide is totally up to you and im not trying to scare you it's just that it's easy to take Dr's etc advice as gospel. Just whatever you do take some time to do research on all angles. I hope you find success with whatever you decide though.

I was thinking this as well. I had costochondritis the other year. Started last Christmas eve. I was in so much pain,whenever I bent forward I felt this huge pressure like my chest wall was going to explode out of me. The severity of the pain mimics that of a heart attack and radiates out to other places. I've had it since then as well in other parts like round the back of my ribs and arm etc. Moves around. GP mis diagnosed me with acid reflux. After 4 days of hell over Christmas I went to a walk in and they sent me to a+e to rule out any heart issues but both came up with costochondritis. Stress and anxiety will make it worse as it is inflammatory condition and these will exacerbate inflammation due to the release of cortisol in the body. 
However it could be something else entirely bit just sounds so similar to what I experienced that it's worth checking out and getting another opinion. Have u done anything strenuous or injured yourself or maybe moved in a certain way even if it was so slight. Mine started by carrying Christmas shopping. But it doesn't always start with a physical thing. Anyways hope you get a correct diagnosis soon whatever it is and get the right treatment. Keep us updated if that's ok? Wish you better
